failures.question: For each month from February 2011 to November 2011, what was the percentage change in revenue versus the previous month?
failures.example_sql:
WITH monthly_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
        d.year,
        d.month,
        d.month_start,
        SUM(s.revenue) AS revenue
    FROM fact_sales s
    JOIN dim_date d ON s.date_key = d.date_key
    WHERE s.invoice_date >= '2011-02-01' AND s.invoice_date < '2011-12-01'
    GROUP BY d.year, d.month, d.month_start
),
revenue_with_lag AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        month,
        month_start,
        revenue,
        LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY year, month) AS prev_revenue
    FROM monthly_revenue
)
SELECT 
    to_char(month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month_name,
    revenue,
    prev_revenue,
    CASE 
        WHEN prev_revenue IS NULL OR prev_revenue = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND(((revenue - prev_revenue) / prev_revenue) * 100.0, 2)
    END AS percentage_change
FROM revenue_with_lag
ORDER BY year, month

failures.question: What was our net revenue in 2011 after cancellations?
failures.example_sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(s.revenue), 0) + COALESCE(SUM(c.revenue), 0) AS net_revenue FROM dim_date d LEFT JOIN fact_sales s ON d.date_key = s.date_key AND s.invoice_date >= '2011-01-01' AND s.invoice_date < '2012-01-01' LEFT JOIN fact_cancellations c ON d.date_key = c.date_key AND c.invoice_date >= '2011-01-01' AND c.invoice_date < '2012-01-01' WHERE d.year = 2011

failures.question: Which 5 customers had the highest net revenue after cancellations, and what was it?
failures.example_sql: SELECT c.customer_id, COALESCE(SUM(s.revenue), 0) + COALESCE(SUM(can.revenue), 0) AS net_revenue FROM dim_customer c LEFT JOIN fact_sales s ON c.customer_id = s.customer_id LEFT JOIN fact_cancellations can ON c.customer_id = can.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY net_revenue DESC LIMIT 5
